title.narrative: Improved working conditions of women in the labour market and reducing patterns of discrimination

description.narrative: The ILO collaborates extensively with the Ministry of Labour (MoL), the Jordanian National Commission for Women (JNCW), the Jordan Chamber of Industry (JCI), the General Federation of Jordanian Trade Union (GFJTU), the Social Security Corporation (SSC), and the Inter-Ministerial Committee for Women’s Empowerment to tackle gender and decent work challenges, particularly among women and vulnerable groups. The ILO also participates in various high-level national committees dedicated to promoting gender equality, diversity, and inclusion. This is in support of the national vision as outlined in two key documents: the National Strategy for Women in Jordan (2020-2025) and the Economic Modernization Vision Plan. By 2026, women and men will have better access to a work environment that provides a safe work environment free from violence and harassment, as well as pay equity, maternity and paternity protection, as well as safeguarding night shift workers, Persons with Disabilities (PWD) and pregnant and lactating mothers. Additionally, establishing a quota for women in executive roles and on boards of directors. Efforts are underway by the ILO to develop tools and platforms that enable the Government of Jordan to enforce the legislation and assist employers in complying with these mandates. The outcome will contribute to the advancement of gender equality and sustainable development in Jordan, as well as in the Arab region by increasing evidence-based knowledge products, facilitating knowledge exchange, and building Arab narratives and approaches for strengthening the care economy that would pave the ways to start taking concrete measures to realize sustainable development.
